page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure BM.Standard.A4.48 is a bare-metal server powered by the Arm64 Ampere AmpereOne-M processor architecture. The machine provides 96 physical cores operating at a fixed frequency of 3.6 GHz with a single thread per core, delivering 96 dedicated execution contexts without hyperthreading resource contention. This architecture is coupled with 768.0 GB of system memory, providing an 8.0 GB RAM per core allocation ratio. A single complimentary public IPv4 address is included.

For local data persistence, the server includes 3840 GB of integrated NVMe SSD storage, directly attached to bypass external block storage overhead. The absence of a discrete GPU reflects a platform geared toward memory-heavy and compute-intensive non-accelerated workloads. The single-threaded core design offers consistent execution predictability, preventing noisy-neighbor effects commonly found in simultaneous multithreading environments.

The 1:8 core-to-memory ratio paired with bare-metal NVMe storage delivers high resource density. From an operational efficiency perspective, the high core count and dedicated hardware profile lower virtualization overhead and offer sustained performance for horizontally scalable tasks. The platform is well suited for in-memory databases, large-scale caching tiers, container orchestration engines, continuous integration build clusters, and data processing pipelines.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure BM.Standard.A4.48 is a bare-metal compute instance built on the 64-bit Arm Ampere AmpereOne-M architecture. It provides 96 physical cores at 3.6 GHz with single-threaded execution, ensuring 96 dedicated vCPUs free from hyperthreading contention. The server features 768.0 GB of RAM, offering an allocation of 8.0 GB per core that caters to high-footprint workloads. Integrated storage is provisioned via 3840 GB of local NVMe SSD capacity, providing fast access to temporary and scratch data without network transport layers. The instance does not include discrete GPUs and includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. Its balanced combination of massive physical core counts, high memory density, and low-latency local solid-state storage makes BM.Standard.A4.48 an effective deployment target for large in-memory key-value databases, container orchestration nodes, memory-bound analytics pipelines, and intensive multithreaded build systems.
